records.title: Instrument flight and radio-navigation infrastructure
records.sourceNativeSummary: Doolittle’s 1929 blind-flight demonstration showed that gyro horizon, sensitive altimeter and radio/navigation aids could replace outside visual reference for key phases of flight. Later airway/radio-navigation infrastructure turned instrument capability into routine all-weather operations.
records.rivalOrBoundary: One instrument is not instrument flight: reliable performance required multiple displays, calibrated ground/radio infrastructure, procedures and pilot training; failures could arise from mismatched or misleading instruments.

sources.supports: sensitive altimeter type used by Doolittle

records.title: Stored blood and blood-bank systems through wartime transfusion
records.sourceNativeSummary: Citrate/storage methods and later plasma separation/logistics converted transfusion from immediate donor-to-patient practice into a distributed collection, preservation, testing and delivery system. Charles Drew’s Blood for Britain work helped standardize large-scale blood/plasma banking during WWII.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Plasma portability did not make it equivalent to whole blood, and early pooled products carried contamination/infection risks. Institutional racial segregation of blood also shows technically effective infrastructure can embed scientifically invalid social policy.

sources.supports: plasma preservation/storage and Blood for Britain
scientifically invalid racial segregation policy in wartime blood programs

records.title: Sulfonamide antibacterial therapy before penicillin scale
records.sourceNativeSummary: Domagk’s Prontosil work demonstrated systemic antibacterial chemotherapy in animal infection models and became the basis for sulfonamide drugs before penicillin was clinically scalable.
records.rivalOrBoundary: A drug-class breakthrough did not establish universal efficacy or safety; organism, dose, toxicity and resistance differ, and sulfonamides remained a serious comparator rather than a superseded mistake during early penicillin work.

sources.supports: 1932 Prontosil antibacterial effects and sulfa-drug foundation

records.title: Yellow-fever 17D vaccine development and deployment
records.sourceNativeSummary: Yellow-fever virus was attenuated through laboratory passage in the 1930s, producing the 17D lineage that became a durable vaccine platform for endemic/travel protection.
records.rivalOrBoundary: The useful vaccine emerged from attenuation and field/clinical evidence, not a complete molecular understanding. Different vaccine strains had different adverse-event profiles, so “yellow-fever vaccine” is not one timeless risk object.

sources.supports: 1930s vaccine development, 17D/French neurotropic lineages and safety differences

records.title: Birdseye quick freezing and frozen-food cold-chain commercialization
records.sourceNativeSummary: Birdseye’s 1920s work used rapid small-quantity freezing, tighter packaging and later dedicated freezer/distribution practices to preserve food quality better than slow freezing. Commercial acceptance required stores/freezers and consumer demonstration, not process chemistry alone.
records.rivalOrBoundary: A good preservation method can remain commercially weak without cold-chain infrastructure, retail equipment and consumer trust; later freezer ubiquity must not be back-projected into the initial action surface.

sources.supports: Birdseye quick-freezing, packaging, retailer freezer/consignment and consumer-adoption barriers

records.title: British National Grid and system-level electrical coordination
records.sourceNativeSummary: Britain’s grid build connected regional generation through a common high-voltage transmission substrate. Regional grid operation began in 1933 and became a synchronized national system in 1938, changing balancing/reserve and generation-location possibilities.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Interconnection value depended on common frequency/operating coordination and justified capital only at system scale; a grid can also centralize failure/authority and create path dependence.

sources.supports: 1928 first pylon, 1933 regional operation and 1938 national grid synchronization

records.title: TVA/Hoover multi-purpose hydroelectric and regional-development infrastructure
records.sourceNativeSummary: Large dams and TVA combined electricity with flood control, navigation, land/resource management and regional development. TVA’s 1933 statutory objective was multi-dimensional by construction, not a pure generation project.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Power output alone cannot grade such systems. Reservoir displacement, land authority, ecological changes, navigation and regional distributional effects belong to the same consequence boundary.

sources.supports: unified river system for flood control, navigation and electricity
